newsitem.title: UK: UK COURT TELLS CO-OP PREDATOR TO RETURN DOCUMENTS.
newsitem.headline: UK COURT TELLS CO-OP PREDATOR TO RETURN DOCUMENTS.

text.p: The London High Court on Friday ordered Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica and its head Andrew Regan to disclose any confidential information they may have about its takeover target, the Co-Operative Wholesale Society.
The move followed an application by the Co-op which on Thursday suspended two senior executives, Allan Green and David Chambers for an alleged serious breach of trust.

The court order prohibits Lanica, its offshoot Galileo Ltd, Regan, Lanica director and former CWS adviser David Lyons and Green from using any confidential material they may have and requires them to provide sworn affidavits by 1500 GMT on Tuesday April 22 detailing what information has been disclosed.
The court also ordered that the use to which the information has been put should be disclosed and that the information must be returned to CWS.

Regan has been stalking CWS as a prospective buy for some time and there has been intense speculation this week that he was about to launch a 1.0 billion pounds bid for the non-retail businesses of CWS which include the profitable Co-operative Bank and insurance, funeral and travel businesses.
Regan is thought to want to break-up CWS as a result of the recent poor overall performance of the group which earlier this week reported a fall in profits for 1996.
